ConnectTracker.description:
`POST /api/projects/{project}/trackers`: connect a Plane project. A
project's owner or editor may. `project` is Plane's project id or its
identifier. Control reads the project with the key first: a key Plane
refuses or a project it doesn't know is a 422 and nothing is kept. The
key and the webhook secret are sealed and never come back.

created.description: False when an `import_key` named one made before.

authorize.description: `via: "browser"`: GitHub's page to open; the draft isn't sent yet.

machine.description: The machine's name, when one sent it.

via.description:
How it went: `token` (as the person, through GitHub's authorization)
or `machine`.

head_sha.description: The head commit they're on; `None` for an issue.

comments.description:
Comments, reviews' text and review comments, oldest first. A review
comment's thread is the ones whose `reply_to` is its `id`.

from.description: `github` (read now, or a few minutes ago) or `mirror`.

agent.description:
The agent that wrote it, and the machine it was on (an id, and its
name when the machine is still there).

author.description: The person it's for: an account id.

id.description: The platform's id: `dft_` and 32 hex characters.

item.description: The mirrored item it's on, and its title, when the mirror has it.

actor.description: Who did it: a GitHub login.

ForgeItem.description:
A PR or an issue, as metadata: never its body. A Plane item (#420) is
one too, with `provider` `plane`.

id.description: The platform's id: `fi_` and 32 hex characters.

number.description: A Plane item's sequence id (`ALL-2212` is 2212).

provider.description: `github` or `plane`; an older platform's items are GitHub's.

state_name.description:
A Plane item's state as Plane names it (`In Review`) and its group
(`backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed` or `cancelled`).

url.description: A Plane item's page in Plane.

project.description: The project's id (`personal` asked is answered with the real one).

withheld.description:
The project's linked repos whose items the reader may not see, and
why: their names are the project's, which its members see anyway.

login.description:
M172: the reader's GitHub login, when it's linked for them: who
"you" are to a block pinned to one of its items, which reads no
GitHub of its own.

merge_styles.description:
`merge` method's words (`merge`, `squash`, `rebase`), read from
GitHub with the App and kept an hour, for a block pinned to one of
its items, which reads no GitHub of its own. Absent until known;
empty when GitHub won't say.
merge_styles.title: 427: the ways the repository lets a pull request be merged, in the

project.description: The project it's linked to, when it's linked for the reader.

ForgeText.description: A body, a comment, a review's text or a review comment.

id.description: GitHub's id: the PR's or issue's for a body.

path.description: A review comment's file and line.

author.description: A GitHub login; a native issue's author's name.

created_at.description: When it came into the inbox, and when the item last changed.

item.description:
The item: `fi_` and 32 hex characters, a native issue's `iss_` id
(M202), or a run's `run_` id (M215).

project.description: A native issue's or a run's project (M202, M215).

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME`; a native issue's or a run's project's name.

room.description: A `thread_mention`'s room: the thread on the item (M202).

url.description:
The item on GitHub; a native issue's or a run's path on the
platform page (`/issues/<id>`, `/runs/<id>`).

InboxMark.description:
Mark an item's entries: `true` sets seen or done (now, if it wasn't),
`false` clears it, and one not given stays as it is.

reason.description: Only this reason's entry; all of the item's when `None`.

InboxShadow.description:
What an opted-in machine's forge blocks want of its owner (the shadow
period, M171): items and reasons, never a title.

LinkRepo.description:
`POST /api/projects/{project}/repos`: link `OWNER/NAME`. A project
member who is an admin or maintainer of it on GitHub may. When the
GitHub App isn't installed where it lives, the answer is a 409 with
`reason: "install_app"` and `install_url`, GitHub's page to install it,
which brings them back to the project's settings.

LinkedRepo.description: A repo linked to a project, or unlinked and waiting for the purge.

linked_by.description: Who linked it (an account id), when that account is still there.

mirror_content.description: The project mirrors its PRs' and issues' bodies and comments (M166).

purge_after.description: When its rows go, unless it's linked again first.

unlinked_at.description: When it was unlinked: nothing is read from GitHub for it since.

project.description: The project's id (`personal` asked is answered with the real one).

Me.description: The signed-in person, as the hub knows them.

name.description: The name it chose, else its login, else "".

NewDraft.description:
A draft to make. From a person (their own), or from a machine (an
agent's on it, for its owner: the platform records the machine, and
`agent` names the agent).

agent.description: The agent that wrote it (`mcp:claude-code`), from a machine.

import_key.description:
A machine's own id for a draft it kept and now uploads: the same
key makes no second draft, and is answered with the first. Only a
machine gives one.

number.description: The PR or issue; `None` for a new issue.

repo.description: `OWNER/NAME`: a repo linked to a project the author is in.

team.description: The team it's the default project of; `None` for the person's own.

role.description: The reader's role in it: `owner`, `editor` or `viewer`.

hosted.description:
Hosted workspaces are open to this person (M179's allowlist): only
then does the shell offer to delegate a project to control (M178).
A platform from before leaves it out.

RepoSettings.description:
`PATCH /api/projects/{project}/repos/{owner}/{name}` (M166): a linked
repo's settings; the answer is its [`LinkedRepo`]. `mirror_content`
on keeps its PRs' and issues' bodies and comments on the platform
(search finds their text); off deletes them at once. Turning it on
takes what linking takes: a member who maintains the repo on GitHub.

back.description: For `browser`: the platform page's path to come back to.

drafts.description:
The platform's waiting drafts the block shows (`dft_` ids): its
`draft` reason, when one is the owner's.

reasons.description:
What the block's attention rules find now, as [`INBOX_REASONS`]
(`draft` aside), whether or not the person looked.

compared.description: Blocks on items the platform has, and how many agreed.

explained.description:
Differences the platform can't help by design (a mention where
content isn't mirrored): not in `compared`.

TrackerClose.description: How a tracker item is closed.

TrackerConnection.description:
A tracker project connected to a project, or disconnected and waiting
for the purge. Never the key or the webhook secret.

agent_writes.description:
A summary for a client that predates `write_policy`: `allow` if every
kind of agent write is allowed, else `approve`. Read-only.

attribution.description: What a write's footer says: `full`, `short` or `none`.

backfilled_at.description: When the first read of its items finished.

has_webhook_secret.description: A webhook secret is kept for it.

identifier.description: The project's short key, such as `ARUGU`.

items.description: How many of its items the platform holds.

last_delivery_at.description: When a signed delivery from Plane last arrived.

linked_by.description: Who connected it (an account id), when that account is still there.

purge_after.description: When its rows go, unless it's connected again first.

source_project_id.description: The tracker's own id for the project (Plane's uuid).

unlinked_at.description: When it was disconnected: nothing is read from the tracker for it since.

waiting_writes.description: Agents' writes waiting for a person to approve.

webhook_url.description: The payload URL to give Plane's webhook for it.

write_policy.description: Which kinds of agent write go at once and which wait for a person.

project.description: The project's id (`personal` asked is answered with the real one).

TrackerFieldName.description: A module, a type or a label of a Plane project.

TrackerFieldState.description: A state of a Plane project, as `tracker.fields` lists them.

default.description: The state a new item starts in.

TrackerFields.description:
What a connected Plane project offers a work item (#422): the names a
[`TrackerWrite`] may use.

connection.description: The connection (`tc_…`) and its identifier, such as `ARUGU`.

read_at.description: When control last read them from Plane (milliseconds).

states.description: In the order Plane keeps them.

types.description: Empty when the project doesn't have item types.

TrackerPendingWrite.description: A write waiting for a person, as the Triage page shows it.

error.description: Why it failed, in a sentence.

person.description: Whose agent, and on which machine.

target.description: `IDENT-N` of the item it targets, or none for a new item.

write.description: The write, as it will be sent (without the footer).

TrackerReach.description:
The projects a machine holds `trackers.write` over, as its owner reads
them now.

TrackerReachConnection.description: A live Plane connection of a project an agent reaches.

agent_writes.description: `allow` if every kind of write is allowed, else `approve`.

connections.description: Its live connections: never a key or a secret.

TrackerSettings.description:
`PATCH /api/projects/{project}/trackers/{connection}`: which kinds of
agent write wait for a person (`write_policy`), what their footer says
(`attribution`: `full`, `short` or `none`), the older `agent_writes`
(`approve` or `allow`, which sets every kind), and the webhook secret;
any of them, the answer is its
[`TrackerConnection`]. A webhook secret is sealed like the key and never
shown back; an empty one removes it.

TrackerWrite.description:
A write to a tracker's work item, the same for people and agents. `item`
is the mirror's `fi_` id, or `IDENT-N` (the connection's identifier and
the item's number). Assignees are not here: a tracker's members aren't
Arugula's people.

oneOf.description:
A new item. On an agent's route `connection` or `tracker` (the
connection's identifier, in any case) says where; with neither, the
project's only live connection is used. On a person's, the path's
connection is it. `state` is a state's name or id, or a state group
(`backlog`, `unstarted`, `started`, `completed`, `cancelled`: its
first state); `state_group` is the same, as an older daemon sends
it. `module`, `type` and `labels` are names or ids and `parent` is
`IDENT-N`; control turns them into the tracker's ids when it sends
the write.
Open it again, in the project's default state.

Change an item: what is `None` or empty stays. The fields are a
create's; `labels` are added and `labels_remove` taken off.

TrackerWriteDone.description:
What a write came to: it landed (`sent`, with the item's `fi_` id), or
it waits for a person (`waiting`, with its `tw_` id).

item.description:
The mirror row the write reached or made (`fi_` and hex), and its
`IDENT-N`.

write.description: The waiting write's id (`tw_` and hex).

TrackerWritePolicy.description:
What an agent's write to a tracker does, per kind: `allow` sends it at
once, `approve` keeps it for a person. An edit that is several kinds goes
at once only if every one of them allows.

create.description: A new work item, whatever fields it carries.

edit.description: An edit of the title or the body.

fields.description: An edit naming a module, parent, type or labels.

state.description: A close, a reopen, or an edit naming a state.

why.description:
`no_github` (the reader didn't sign in to control with GitHub),
`no_access` (GitHub doesn't give them access), `busy` (too many
lookups lately: it shows again within the hour) or `no_app` (this
control has no GitHub App to ask with).
